nodes.summary: Let $n > 1$ be a composite natural number. Then the number of integers $b$ with $1 \le b < n$ such that $n$ is a Fermat pseudoprime to the base $b$, that is, $b^{n-1} \equiv 1 \pmod{n}$, equals $\prod_p \gcd(n - 1, p - 1)$, where $p$ runs over the distinct prime divisors of $n$.
nodes.title: Number of Fermat pseudoprime bases (Monier; Baillie–Wagstaff)

Write $d$ for the odd part of $n - 1$ and $d_p$ for the odd part of $p - 1$. nodes.title: Monier's formula for the number of strong pseudoprime bases

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a natural number such that the Fermat number $F_k = 2^{2^k} + 1$ is composite. Then for every natural number $t$, $F_k$ is a strong pseudoprime to both bases $2^{2^{k-1}+t} + 2^t$ and $2^{2^{k-1}+t} - 2^t$, computed modulo $F_k$.
nodes.title: Strong pseudoprime bases $2^{2^{k-1}+t} \pm 2^t$ of composite Fermat numbers

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a natural number such that the Fermat number $F_k = 2^{2^k} + 1$ is composite. Then for every integer $t$, $F_k$ is a strong pseudoprime to the base $2^t$, where the power is taken in the unit group of $\mathbb{Z}/F_k\mathbb{Z}$ (in which $2$ is a unit because $F_k$ is odd).
nodes.title: Composite Fermat numbers are strong pseudoprimes to every power of $2$

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a natural number such that the Fermat number $F_k = 2^{2^k} + 1$ is composite, and let $S_k$ be the set of residues modulo $F_k$ of the form $2^t$, $2^{2^{k-1}+t} + 2^t$ or $2^{2^{k-1}+t} - 2^t$ with $t$ a natural number. Then the units of $\mathbb{Z}/F_k\mathbb{Z}$ that lie in $S_k$ form a subgroup of the unit group of order $2^{k+2}$, and $F_k$ is a strong pseudoprime to every base in $S_k$.
nodes.title: A subgroup of strong pseudoprime bases of a composite Fermat number

nodes.title: The subgroup criteria for strong pseudoprime bases hold almost always

nodes.summary: The set of odd composite natural numbers $n$ for which the units $b$ of $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ such that $n$ is a strong pseudoprime to the base $b$ do not form a subgroup of the unit group has natural density $0$.
nodes.title: Strong pseudoprime bases almost always form a subgroup

nodes.summary: Let $p$ and $q$ be distinct primes. Then the number of integers $b$ with $1 \le b < pq$ such that $pq$ is a Fermat pseudoprime to the base $b$, that is, $b^{pq-1} \equiv 1 \pmod{pq}$, is a perfect square.
nodes.title: Products of two distinct primes have a square number of Fermat pseudoprime bases

nodes.summary: The number $2047 = 23 \cdot 89$ is a strong pseudoprime to the base $2$.
nodes.title: 2047 is a strong pseudoprime to base 2

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number and $b$ a residue class modulo $n$. Then $n$ is a strong pseudoprime to the base $b$ if and only if $n > 1$, $n$ is not prime, $n$ is odd, and there are natural numbers $k$ and $d$ with $n - 1 = 2^k d$ and $d$ odd such that $b^d = 1$ or $b^{2^i d} = -1$ in $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ for some $i < k$.
nodes.title: Unfolded definition of strong pseudoprimes

nodes.summary: Composite divisors of primitive parts without their intrinsic factor are strong pseudoprimes. Let $b > 1$ and $m > 2$ be natural numbers, and let $\Phi_j$ denote the $j$-th cyclotomic polynomial. If a composite natural number $c > 1$ divides $\Phi_m(b) / \gcd(\Phi_m(b), m)$ or $\Phi_{2m}(b) / \gcd(\Phi_{2m}(b), m)$, then $c$ is a strong pseudoprime to the base $b$.
nodes.title: Composite divisors of primitive parts without their intrinsic factor are strong pseudoprimes

nodes.summary: Every odd composite number $n$ is a strong pseudoprime to the base $1$.
nodes.title: Every odd composite is a strong pseudoprime to base 1

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number and $b$ a unit of $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ such that $n$ is a strong pseudoprime to the base $b$. Then for every integer $t$, $n$ is a strong pseudoprime to the base $b^t$, and $n$ is a strong pseudoprime to the base $-b$.
nodes.title: Strong pseudoprime bases are closed under powers and negation

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number and $b$ a residue class modulo $n$. Then $n$ is a strong pseudoprime to the base $b$ if $n$ is an odd composite number (that is, $n > 1$, $n$ is odd and $n$ is not prime) and there are natural numbers $k$ and $d$ with $d$ odd and $n - 1 = 2^k d$ such that either $b^d = 1$ or $b^{2^i d} = -1$ for some $i < k$, where the powers are computed in $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$.

nodes.summary: If $n$ is a strong pseudoprime to some base $b$ modulo $n$, then $n$ is not prime.
nodes.title: Strong pseudoprimes are not prime

nodes.title: Strong pseudoprimes are odd

nodes.title: Strong pseudoprimes exceed one

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
